results.corrected_title: Dutch government plans to cut about 25,000 civil-service jobs, citing AI-driven productivity
results.corrected_summary: On 26 October the Dutch government said it will cut about 25,000 central-government jobs. The announcement came in a statement and a letter to parliament from State Secretary Eric van den Burg. Savings are put at EUR 900m a year by 2027, rising to EUR 3.5bn a year from 2035. The government names AI-driven productivity gains as a main justification.
key_facts: About 25,000 civil-service jobs to be cut
Savings of EUR 900m a year by 2027, rising to EUR 3.5bn a year from 2035
Civil service reached a record 160,000 officials at the end of 2025, up 41% from 2018
Ministries, inspectorates and implementing agencies face cuts of 45% or even 60%; police and defence are exempt
Cabinet will present its AI deployment plans early next year

results.corrected_title: Anthropic study: analysts matched an AI agent's randomly assigned lean in 86% of analytical choices
results.corrected_summary: Anthropic published a randomized trial on 27 October. 61 professional analysts with causal-inference experience were recruited and 50 used the Claude Code agent. The agent was secretly assigned a coin-flip lean on four analytical choices and argued for it. Analysts' choices matched the lean 86% of the time against about 50% expected by chance. 77% repeated the agent's arguments but only 15% credited it. Anthropic says the study covers one task, one field and one model.
key_facts: 61 analysts recruited; 11 chose not to use the agent, so the main analysis covers 50
86% of choices matched the agent's lean, against a 50% chance baseline
77% repeated the agent's arguments in at least one post-task answer; 15% credited the agent
Fictional farming cooperative task with four analytical choices
Anthropic deliberately strengthened the agent's lean to make the effect measurable (per AI Weekly)

results.corrected_title: Bloomberg introduces BQuant Assistant, an AI coding assistant for Python and BQL
results.corrected_summary: On 28 October Bloomberg announced BQuant Assistant, a conversational AI coding assistant inside BQuant. It generates BQL and PyBQL queries across more than 22,000 data fields and can explain and debug code. It runs code in the BQuant sandbox only after user approval. It is generally available in BQuant Enterprise and in limited beta in BQuant Desktop from the end of October.
key_facts: Over 22,000 data fields across equities, fixed income, FX, commodities, indices, ETFs and derivatives
Code is inserted and run in the BQuant sandbox only after user approval
GA in BQuant Enterprise; limited beta in BQuant Desktop at the end of October 2026

results.corrected_title: Meta launches its Muse personal AI agent in Singapore with Gmail, Instagram, Grab and Shopee connectors
results.corrected_summary: Meta's newsroom post is dated 27 October and says Muse is available in Singapore on iOS, Android and muse.ai. Users can connect Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram. Eight local launch partners include Shopee, Grab, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, ShopBack, Klook, Trip.com and Lazada. Connector features roll out progressively.
key_facts: Meta's announcement is dated 2026-10-27, with media coverage on 28 October
Available in Singapore on iOS, Android and muse.ai
Connectors for Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram
Eight local partners: Shopee, Grab, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, ShopBack, Klook, Trip.com, Lazada
